title: Growing up in Brooklyn over his father's ether-filled practice
summary: Schremp opens the interview; Handy was born in Brooklyn, his father a doctor doing ear operations, which inspired the title 'Tonsillectomy'.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I will sort of prompt you and push you along and ask questions and try not to put my priceless opinions in here, although it is very difficult for me to keep out of an interview; it's one of my terrible habits.
I was born in Brooklyn, yes, but you want to know about my early life? You wanted to know about the beginning of Raeburn; didn't you?
No, this is George Handy. This has nothing to do with Raeburn. This is George Handy.
I'm in Brooklyn, smelling ether all day long, from morning till night. My father was a doctor and he performed-- what do you call it--the ear operations--mastoids,
That was the genesis of that title.
Yeah, well--tonsillectomy, out of respect for my father, to actually let him know he was a part of my thoughts in my music somewhere, so I titled it 'Tonsillectomy'.
Lorraine said you referred to him as the 'tonsil doctor'?
Yeah, he was, they used to line up to have their throats cut by my father.
Anyway, the apartment smelled of ether, it got so I could live in a world of ether without being affected by it.
That was in the beginning, and then we moved upstairs and I didn't escape from the ether, it seeped through the ceiling into where we were living.
